As for the complaints, they are as follows: It is a low state for a woman to be a common object, so that if one person enters and another also enters, they will undoubtedly kill one another. What was said—that one must pay five hundred <term>karshapana</term> <gloss>ancient Indian coins</gloss> to enter—is also true; it is necessary for her clothing and adornments without doubt.

What was said—that the house must be vacated after seven days—is also true; whether it is done sooner or later, what conflict is there in that? What was said—that one does not inquire about the coming and going of men—is also true; because this is a courtesan, if one were to inquire about the coming and going of all the men, who would ever enter her house?

Then, the assembly granted her the five supreme conditions, and she began to be enjoyed by the assembly. As the Licchavis of Vaishali began to enter her house to enjoy themselves as they wished, some, due to an intense attachment to worldly things, became free of desire the moment they saw her. Others were satisfied by mere touch, and none of them performed the act of a man. She thought, "Since these are not men, I must prepare a strategy." Having settled in various places,

<leaf-break/>

there was one named Amrapali, who possessed perfect beauty and youth, and was skilled in the sixty-four arts; she was a woman worthy of being enjoyed by the gods alone. She said, "Your Majesty, if that is the case, I shall go to Vaishali and enjoy myself with him as I please." The King said, "The Licchavis of Vaishali have long been enemies who cause harm and strike back; they will bring harm upon you." The King said, "Wise ones, these men are brave in heart, so I will go." She said, "Your Majesty, if you insist on a matter that has no purpose, then you may go." She boarded a chariot and set out for Vaishali with the King. Gradually arriving in Vaishali, the King stayed in the pleasure grove.

The King entered Amrapali's house, and after a short time, the sound of a bell arose. The Licchavis of Vaishali became agitated and said, "Wise ones, a person who is not our friend has entered, and the bell has rung." As the sound became clear and grew loud, King Bimbisara asked Amrapali, "Lovely one, what is this?" "Your Majesty, someone is checking the residence." "For what reason?" "For your sake." "What shall we do? Shall we flee?" "Your Majesty, do not be displeased. Your Majesty, when seven days have passed and..."

He played with her, delighted with her, and enjoyed himself as he pleased. After some time, Amrapali became pregnant and said to King Bimbisara, "Your Majesty, I am with child." He gave her a piece of linen and a signet ring, saying, "If it is a girl, it is yours. They said, "Wise ones, the enemy has appeared, so follow and search!" As five hundred Licchavis with arrow-spoke wheels pursued King Bimbisara, the King saw them and said, "Your Majesty, if the Licchavis of Vaishali are coming, will you fight them, or shall I drive the chariot?" and said, "Wise ones, the one who is our enemy is the father of this child," and they struck him even more fiercely. As she sat thinking such thoughts, she saw many merchants loaded with goods heading toward Rajagriha. She said, "Take this signet ring; by showing it, you will obtain passage and will not be charged tolls. <translation page="214">A Bodhisattva is not one who is absorbed in their own mind, nor is one who is absorbed in the minds of others. Why is that? Because in this way, the Bodhisattva's mental continuum is known by wisdom. The mental continuum is known by mindfulness. It is known by intellect. The mental continuum is known by realization. The mental continuum is known by discriminative wisdom. The mental continuum is known by sagacity. The mental continuum is devoid of mental afflictions, the connections of karmic imprints are perfectly severed, pure, stainless, luminous, free from faults, not harsh, free from turbidity, and it is known as the manifestation of all phenomena. It is known as entering the flow of the mental activities of all sentient beings. Shariputra, this is called the Bodhisattva's clairvoyance of others' minds and the perfection of the activity of wisdom. Shariputra, concerning this, what is the clairvoyance of recollecting previous lives in the Bodhisattva's direct realization? What is it that perfects the activity of the wisdom of clairvoyance? Shariputra, in this regard, a Bodhisattva, in all the infinite and boundless world systems of the ten directions, knows the births of all sentient beings: one, two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty,
<leaf-break/>
They also recollect the roots of virtue that arose from previous causes. They also recollect the causes of the roots of virtue of others. They dedicate their own roots of virtue toward awakening. Having also made sentient beings recollect the roots of virtue of other sentient beings, they cause them to generate the mind toward awakening. They also rely on the impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and selflessness of those causes of past happiness and suffering. Relying on impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and selflessness, they are not arrogant due to physical form. They are not arrogant due to wealth. They are not arrogant due to servants. They are not arrogant due to power. They are not arrogant due to a desire for a Universal Monarch. They are not arrogant due to a desire for Indra. They are not arrogant due to a desire for Brahma. They are not arrogant due to a desire for the World Protectors. They are not arrogant due to a desire for all births. They are not those with a mind that desires all pleasures of desire, royal rule, and power, except for those who, for the sake of ripening sentient beings, intentionally take on existence. Relying on impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and selflessness, they...</translation>

<translation page="215">They feel shame and bashfulness regarding the conduct of mental afflictions, and they disparage them. For the sake of their very life, they do not perform actions that would become roots of non-virtue in the present existence. They also fully dedicate and expand those past roots of virtue into the unsurpassable, perfectly complete awakening. In order to gather all present roots of virtue, they abandon discordant dedications and, for the sake of ensuring the uninterrupted continuity of the Buddha lineage, the Dharma lineage, and the Sangha lineage, they dedicate all toward omniscience through the power of generating perfect mindfulness. That mindfulness is also highly blessed by the power of the <term>dharmadhatu</term> <gloss>sphere of reality</gloss>. It is unmoving through supreme correctness. It is uninvestigated due to the completion of <term>dhyana</term> <gloss>meditative absorption</gloss>. It is unharmed due to being highly blessed by <term>shamatha</term> <gloss>calm abiding</gloss>. It is unerring due to being perfectly grasped by <term>vipashyana</term> <gloss>special insight</gloss>. It is not ordinary because of direct realization. Because mindfulness does not deteriorate, there is no forgetfulness.
<leaf-break/>

<translation page="107">One will become immune to all who oppose, are unfriendly, are malignant, or are sinful. On no occasion will fear arise from anyone anywhere, and one will become entirely liberated. Furthermore, one will never be stained by the defilement of sin. If one mixes <term>giwang</term> <gloss>bezoar</gloss> pills with sesame oil, smears them on one's face, and appears before a king, one will be embraced like a child and attain great joy, and all fear of the wrathful king will be pacified. If smeared on one's body, even if one is meant to be killed, weapons will not pierce the body; they will break into pieces. If an arrow is shot, it will not descend upon the body, and the bow will break. If one wears a <term>giwang</term> <gloss>bezoar</gloss> pill around the neck and enters difficult paths in desolate wildernesses, mountains, or dense forests, all fear of bandits, deceivers, thieves, <term>yakshas</term> <gloss>nature spirits</gloss>, <term>rakshasas</term> <gloss>demons</gloss>, humans, non-humans, vicious wild beasts, venomous snakes, and poisons will not arise, and they will not be seen. If worn on the right shoulder, one will be victorious over others in all situations. One will also become a great object of worship in all places. All will possess great power and diligence.
<leaf-break/>
One will be able to summon all those provisions and make them come, and they will come to wherever one requests. If there are many shops of perfume sellers, all the goods of the shops will come. If one snaps one's fingers at the door of a beer seller, all the jars of beer will come. If one snaps one's fingers at the door of a granary, all the grain will be summoned. Upon entering the house of a sugar-maker and touching the machines, all the sugarcane syrup and slabs of raw sugar will come. They will be sent to wherever one requests. If one snaps one's fingers at the city gate during a dark and stormy time, everyone dwelling in the city will be awakened from sleep. If one performs this at an enemy's door, they will be driven away. If one casts this into the house of a weapon-maker, the weapons and armor will become stiff and stuck. If one performs this at a king's gate, all opposing, unfriendly, and malignant beings will be bound, stiffened, and stuck. If one smears it on a conch and blows it from a high place, one will be liberated from all fighting, battles, harm, disputes, sorcery, compounded poisons, toxins, and illnesses in the places where the sound is heard. If one blows it at the city gate, all epidemics, harm, and bad omens</translation>

<translation page="108">...will be pacified as there is no oppression, and one will overwhelm others with one's splendor. If worn on the left shoulder, one will become an object of great favor for all men, women, boys, and girls, and all will desire to look upon one. One will become a great object of worship. Many purposes will be accomplished. If worn on the right calf, one will travel a thousand <term>yojanas</term> <gloss>unit of distance</gloss> without feeling fatigue. If one holds a <term>giwang</term> <gloss>bezoar</gloss> pill in the mouth, recites the "magnetizing iron hook" mantra of white mustard seeds with the right hand, and then performs the action without speaking other words while in a high place, one can scatter white mustard seeds toward the direction where the man, woman, boy, or girl one desires is located, and they will be summoned immediately and will arrive. Even if they are located a hundred <term>yojanas</term> <gloss>unit of distance</gloss> away, they will inevitably arrive within three days without doubt. If one wears a <term>giwang</term> <gloss>bezoar</gloss> pill on the right or left hand, wherever one touches, wealth, grain, jewels, precious stones, pearls, <term>shankhshila</term> <gloss>conch-shell fossil</gloss>, coral, gold, silver, clothing, and ornaments will be summoned and come; whatever one requests will come. If one enters a kitchen and snaps one's fingers at the door of the cooking area, all the cooking and the pots
<leaf-break/>
will be entirely pacified. If one blows it in a cattle pen, all the milk will be extracted. It will go to wherever one requests. If one blows it in a goat or sheep pen, the milk of the goats and sheep will be extracted and will go to wherever one requests. If one blows it in the middle of a large crowd of people, everyone will become naked and all their clothing will be summoned. If one smears it on a clay drum and beats it on a high balcony, all cold, wind, and hail will be bound and dissolved, and they will not cause harm. The hail will be blocked for a hundred <term>yojanas</term> <gloss>unit of distance</gloss> all around. If one blows it in a city or throughout the entire region, all illnesses, epidemics, harm, and violence will be pacified. All fighting, battles, disputes, and quarrels will be thoroughly pacified. One will become immune to all who oppose, are unfriendly, are malignant, or are sinful. On no occasion will fear arise from anyone anywhere, and one will become entirely liberated. Furthermore, one will never be stained by the defilement of sin. If one mixes <term>giwang</term> <gloss>bezoar</gloss> pills with sesame oil, smears them on one's face, and appears before a king, one will be embraced like a child and attain great joy, and all fear of the wrathful king will be pacified. If smeared on one's body, even if one is meant to be killed, weapons will not pierce the body; they will break into pieces. If an arrow is shot, it will not descend upon the body, and the bow will break. If one wears a <term>giwang</term> <gloss>bezoar</gloss> pill around the neck and enters difficult paths in desolate wildernesses, mountains, or dense forests, all fear of bandits, deceivers, thieves, <term>yakshas</term> <gloss>nature spirits</gloss>, <term>rakshasas</term> <gloss>demons</gloss>, humans, non-humans, vicious wild beasts, venomous snakes, and poisons will not arise, and they will not be seen. If worn on the right shoulder, one will be victorious over others in all situations. One will also become a great object of worship in all places. All will possess great power and diligence.
<leaf-break/>
One will be able to summon all those provisions and make them come, and they will come to wherever one requests. If there are many shops of perfume sellers, all the goods of the shops will come. If one snaps one's fingers at the door of a beer seller, all the jars of beer will come. If one snaps one's fingers at the door of a granary, all the grain will be summoned. If one snaps one's fingers at the city gate during a dark and stormy time, everyone dwelling in the city will be awakened from sleep. If one performs this at an enemy's door, they will be driven away. If one casts this into the house of a weapon-maker, the weapons and armor will become stiff and stuck. If one performs this at a king's gate, all opposing, unfriendly, and malignant beings will be bound, stiffened, and stuck. If one smears it on a conch and blows it from a high place, one will be liberated from all fighting, battles, harm, disputes, sorcery, compounded poisons, toxins, and illnesses in the places where the sound is heard. If one blows it at the city gate, all epidemics, harm, and bad omens

<translation page="352">
[… ] prepared. Medicines are to be eaten. Water is to be drunk constantly. One who is not overcome by the influence of old age and death will constantly be protected. From the hair of a thief, a crest is made.
One should apply the <term>Hum</term> syllable to it. The skulls of the five Buddhas are seized by the practitioner of yoga. The measure of a skull should be five finger-widths. Having done this, one takes the crest. By the nature of <term>Upaya</term> <gloss>skillful means</gloss> and <term>Prajna</term> <gloss>wisdom</gloss>, the hair-belt is wrapped twice. One wears ash for the sake of offering to the hair. The practitioner of yoga adopts this conduct. The sound of the small drum is the recitation.
The <term>Khatvanga</term> <gloss>ritual staff</gloss> is the meditation on wisdom. By the conduct of the <term>Vajra</term> skull, these are recited and meditated upon. Greed, ignorance, fear, and anger; the fruit of shame is entirely abandoned.
Having abandoned the duality by oneself, one should practice conduct without doubt. Having given the gift of the body, one subsequently practices the conduct properly. Because one has discriminated between those who are worthy and unworthy,
therefore, one should not give gifts. Likewise, food and drink; one should eat whatever is obtained. For the sake of conceptualization regarding what is desirable and undesirable, one should not develop attachment. The conduct of eating and non-eating, likewise, drinking and non-drinking, walking and non-walking; the <term>mantrin</term> <gloss>mantra practitioner</gloss> should not make these into conceptualizations. Which disciple has attained the <term>siddhi</term> <gloss>accomplishment</gloss>? Truly...
<leaf-break/>
regarding clothing, the three-pointed <gloss>staff</gloss> is explained. Regarding one who shows the breasts, that boundary is explained. Regarding one who shows the teeth, that mouth is explained. Regarding one who shows a frown, one should say to loosen the hair. Regarding one who shows the forehead, that back is explained. Regarding one who shows the soles of the feet, one should play with the heels. By the response of the <term>Mudra</term> to the <term>Mudra</term>, one is separated by the <term>Samaya</term> <gloss>vow</gloss>. To that, the Yogini said: "Ema! Son, great is the compassion." If one shows the garland in the hand, it is said that one should gather. If the garland is explicitly offered, the conduct is good and stays within the <term>Samaya</term>. That which is gathered as external is the field of good conduct. To that, the Yogini said: "Whatever is spoken, one should do exactly that." "O Blessed One, what are the gathering places?" The Blessed One replied: "Places, near-places, fields, near-fields, <term>Chandohas</term> <gloss>sacred sites</gloss>, near-<term>Chandohas</term>, likewise gatherings and near-gatherings, <term>Athung-chod</term> <gloss>eating/cutting places</gloss> and near-<term>Athung-chod</term>, charnel grounds and near-charnel grounds. These are the twelve sites, the protectors who are the lords of the ten stages. This should not be told to others. O Blessed One, the places..."</translation>
<translation page="353">
and so on, what are they?" The Blessed One replied: "The site is explained as <term>Jalandhara</term>. Likewise, <term>Oddiyana</term>. The site is <term>Kollagiri</term>.
Likewise, it is <term>Kamru</term>. The near-site is mentioned as <term>Malava</term>. It is the city of <term>Sindhu</term>. The field is explained as <term>Mummuni</term>. The field is the number of those who perform. <term>Devikota</term> is likewise a field.
The field is the number of the <term>Lchak-pa</term> <gloss>those who grasp</gloss>. The near-field is mentioned as <term>Kuluta</term>. Likewise, <term>Arbuta</term>, and the mountain of <term>Khaba</term>, the giver of the best of speech. The near-fields are summarized. The <term>Chandoha</term> is <term>Harikela</term>, and those born in the salt sea, <term>Lampaka</term> and <term>Kanchi</term>. Likewise, <term>Surashtra</term>. The near-<term>Chandoha</term> is <term>Kalinga</term>. The island endowed with gold, and <term>Konkana</term> are also near-<term>Chandohas</term>. I shall speak of them in summary. The <term>Athung-chod</term> city and those situated at the edge of the <term>Athung-chod</term> village are <term>Caritra</term> and <term>Kosala</term>, the city of <term>Bindha-zhonu</term>. The <term>Vajra-garbha</term> of great compassion; the near-<term>Athung-chod</term> are those. The charnel ground, the perfect gathering, and the shore of the charnel-ground ocean. The bank of the pond in the pleasure grove, these are spoken of as near-charnel grounds. For the sake of all sentient beings, the <term>Vajra</term> of the <term>Yogini Tantra</term>. The good gathering of the Yogini, even during the day...
<leaf-break/>
sentient beings come under the power of those. This is the seventh chapter, the Chapter on Determining the Signs and Places.
Then, the mandala of the Yogini will be explained. In the space of the sky, one should visualize the <term>Bhaga</term> <gloss>womb/source</gloss>. In the center, one meditates clearly. The mandala, as previously described, is how the deities arise. The mandala of earth and water is first. Just as is appropriate, the <term>Jinajaya</term> <gloss>fire-eater/Agni</gloss>, and the great wind by the deities, and how the meditator arises, is the mandala born from the <term>Chos-byung</term> <gloss>source of phenomena</gloss>. The two additions are without fault. One arises from the central seed. It is said to be the exterior of the triangle. Inside that, one should visualize the essence of the fifteen dead on the seat. Above that is the moon. Above the moon is the seed syllable. Subsequently, one is pressed by the victor over the demons. From the bending of the two, great bliss arises. The <term>Ali</term> <gloss>vowels</gloss> dwell in the form of the moon. The <term>Kali</term> <gloss>consonants</gloss> make them appear. From the gathering of the moon and sun, the white [deity] and others are famously known. The moon possesses the mirror-like wisdom. The seventh of the seven possesses equality. The seed and hand-symbol of one's own deity are spoken of as individual discernment. Everything becomes one, the exertion. The perfection is the pure <term>Dharmadhatu</term>. By the ritual spoken by the learned, the five forms..."</translation>

<keywords>Vajra, Yogini, Tantra, Mandalas, Charnel grounds, Sacred geography, Athung-chod, Mudra, Ritual conduct</keywords>

By the <term>Hum</term> syllable and her frowning expression, she destroys the seven levels <note>of the underworld</note>. Homage to the blissful, the virtuous, the peaceful one, who is the field of practice of the peaceful nirvana. <term>Mandara</term> <gloss>a legendary mountain</gloss>, and the <term>Vindhya</term> <gloss>a mountain range</gloss>, and the three worlds are made to tremble. By speaking the two <term>Tare</term> <gloss>a mantra of Tara</gloss> and the <term>Phat</term> <gloss>a syllable of destruction</gloss> syllable, she dispels all poisons without exception. Homage to her who is the king of the hosts of gods, worshipped by gods and <term>Kimnaras</term> <gloss>celestial musicians</gloss>. By the glory of her joyful armor, she dispels quarrels and bad dreams. Homage to her whose two eyes are brightly radiant, like the full sun and moon. By speaking the two <term>Hara</term> <gloss>an epithet of Tara</gloss> and the <term>Tuttare</term> <gloss>a mantra of Tara</gloss>, she dispels the most intense contagious diseases. By this virtuous offering, may they attain Buddhahood. Because the very compassionate Apa Rna-krong has great interest in the Holy Dharma, he established a connection through meal and beer once. May he be born in the field of Avalokiteshvara. May they be born in the presence of Ugyen Pema. The learned master who has held the lineage from before, the teacher Pema Kar, and the two Tagshar-khyipo, offered service to the Dharma with meal and spirits. 

May their merit expand like the horizon of the sky. In the region of the cool-land, Themgangbi, the youth Tagshar Kunzang established a connection to the Dharma with meal and spirits. The Kumuda-flower Karma Wangmo offers her monthly share of spirits to that Dharma. May she become rich in wealth that knows no poverty. The elder of Tsang, the eloquent Khoche Gawa, offered meal and beer once as service to the Dharma. May he be long-lived, healthy, and abundant in wealth. The great practitioner of the expanse of the Great Perfection, who holds the elephant of mindfulness in his mind, the master of the secret-lord Norbu, and together with them the wandering meditator Tenzin Guru, the ascetic meditator Tashi, the meditator Karma who has abandoned worldly thoughts, and the meditator Ngawang Trinle—these individuals offered their merit and offered it to the Holy Dharma. Pema Tsewang, who is great in Dharma, and the pure-visioned Apa Drug Tsering, the very intelligent Apa Drug Phuntshog, and all the Tagshar who are gifted by the heavens, each offered meal and spirits. <translation page="14">Just as that does not become peaceful, you should know that attachment to desires is similar. A person afflicted by leprosy, tormented by the suffering of worms moving under the skin, relies entirely on the warmth of a fire for the sake of comfort. Even though it appears to provide relief for a moment, the illness does not become peaceful; rather, the fever increases due to the serum, and the pain intensifies. Just like that, relying on the qualities of desire may seem satisfying for a moment, but desire subsequently expands and becomes insatiable. Therefore, know that attachment to desires is like that, and you should turn away from the craving that attaches to the objects of desire from the very beginning.

Because that craving expands and there is no satisfaction, immediately after explaining the attachment to desires, we proceed to explain the actual path. Regarding the explanation of the path: this consists of an extensive explanation of the common path and a brief indication of the uncommon Mahayana path and the entrance to the fruit. Regarding the first, there is the identification of what is to be cultivated through a brief instruction, and the explanation of the sequence of the five paths through an extensive explanation. Regarding the first, to see the ultimate truth, one should cultivate the mental engagement that reflects correctly upon objects. There is no other virtuous quality that is similar to that. The purpose is to see and realize the ultimate nature.

<leaf-break/>

Objects composed of form and consciousness are called "conditioned" because they are produced by causes and conditions. Furthermore, because they produce subsequent states moment by moment and the former ones cease, they are impermanent due to constantly changing and disintegrating. In accordance with that, the mental engagement of reflecting correctly is the path; conditioned things other than the Truth of the Path are contaminated. This includes the environment and the inhabitants contained within the three realms, the sense faculties, the body, consciousness, and mental factors. There are five [types of suffering associated with the contaminated]. Those connected with painful feelings are the suffering of suffering. Those connected with pleasant feelings are the suffering of change. Those connected with neutral feelings are the suffering of compositional factors. Furthermore, the suffering of suffering is known even by animals and the like. The suffering of change is seen by individuals possessing wisdom. Although the suffering of compositional factors is the foundation of all suffering, it is not known by others and is only realized by the aryas. The phrase "all phenomena are empty" is often used in a general sense to mean "emptiness free from conceptual elaboration." Here, however, the emptiness of the aspect of the Truth of Suffering means being empty of discordant causes. Therefore, a creator such as Ishvara, or proponents of time as the cause and others, cannot exist in the reality of phenomena. Understanding that it is empty of such a creator, and by conquering the various compatible causes and conditions,

<leaf-break/>

The nature of this—the wisdom, concentration, and ethical discipline that are uncontaminated—possesses the power to abandon afflictions and is what enables the attainment of the state of cessation. Having certainty in that way is the mental engagement with the aspect of the Truth of the Path. Regarding the detailed explanation of the division of the five paths: there are two parts, the instruction on the sequence of the path of ordinary beings and the instruction on the arya path along with its fruit. The first includes the instruction on the qualities associated with the path of accumulation, and the instruction on the qualities associated with the path of preparation. Regarding the first, the instruction that one must rely primarily on ethics and wisdom on the path of accumulation is as follows: Even persons endowed with caste, form, and learning are not respected if they lack wisdom and ethics. Therefore, whoever possesses these two qualities, even if they lack other virtues, is worthy of worship. Whatever persons may have become the king’s caste, like a great sala tree, or the brahmin’s caste, like a great sala tree—thus having become of the highest caste—possessing fine form such as being beautiful and free of illness, and having undergone extensive training in the eighteen sciences and other conventional studies—if they lack the wisdom to act according to the nature of reality and to know the path of liberation, and lack the ethics of abiding in purified conduct of what to accept and what to reject, they are not objects of respect and worship for the world, including the gods. Furthermore, if one has caste, form, and learning...</translation>

<translation page="15">...then what more need be said? Even if they lack other virtues, whoever possesses those two qualities—the wisdom that knows the nature of reality and the path of liberation, and the perfection of ethics—has become a holy object of worship and respect in the world. As for that wisdom, there are three types: the wisdom arising from hearing, the wisdom arising from reflection, and the wisdom arising from meditation. In this context of the path of accumulation, the wisdom arising from hearing and reflection are the most important. Although there are limitless bodhisattva ethics, in this context, it refers to the ethics of individual liberation. <leaf-break/>

Since they will not arrive as companions, one should never perform negative actions for the sake of others. pages.14:
Just as that does not become peaceful, you should know that attachment to desires is similar. A person afflicted by leprosy, tormented by the suffering of worms moving under the skin, relies entirely on the warmth of a fire for the sake of comfort. Even though it appears to provide relief for a moment, the illness does not become peaceful; rather, the fever increases due to the serum, and the pain intensifies. Just like that, relying on the qualities of desire may seem satisfying for a moment, but desire subsequently expands and becomes insatiable. Therefore, know that attachment to desires is like that, and you should turn away from the craving that attaches to the objects of desire from the very beginning.

Because that craving expands and there is no satisfaction, immediately after explaining the attachment to desires, we proceed to explain the actual path. Regarding the explanation of the path: this consists of an extensive explanation of the common path and a brief indication of the uncommon Mahayana path and the entrance to the fruit. Regarding the first, there is the identification of what is to be cultivated through a brief instruction, and the explanation of the sequence of the five paths through an extensive explanation. Regarding the first, to see the ultimate truth, one should cultivate the mental engagement that reflects correctly upon objects. There is no other virtuous quality that is similar to that. The purpose is to see and realize the ultimate nature.

<leaf-break/>

Objects composed of form and consciousness are called "conditioned" because they are produced by causes and conditions. Furthermore, because they produce subsequent states moment by moment and the former ones cease, they are impermanent due to constantly changing and disintegrating. In accordance with that, the mental engagement of reflecting correctly is the path; conditioned things other than the Truth of the Path are contaminated. This includes the environment and the inhabitants contained within the three realms, the sense faculties, the body, consciousness, and mental factors. There are five [types of suffering associated with the contaminated]. Those connected with painful feelings are the suffering of suffering. Those connected with pleasant feelings are the suffering of change. Those connected with neutral feelings are the suffering of compositional factors. Furthermore, the suffering of suffering is known even by animals and the like. The suffering of change is seen by individuals possessing wisdom. Although the suffering of compositional factors is the foundation of all suffering, it is not known by others and is only realized by the aryas. The phrase "all phenomena are empty" is often used in a general sense to mean "emptiness free from conceptual elaboration." Here, however, the emptiness of the aspect of the Truth of Suffering means being empty of discordant causes. Therefore, a creator such as Ishvara, or proponents of time as the cause and others, cannot exist in the reality of phenomena. Understanding that it is empty of such a creator, and by conquering the various compatible causes and conditions,

<leaf-break/>

The nature of this—the wisdom, concentration, and ethical discipline that are uncontaminated—possesses the power to abandon afflictions and is what enables the attainment of the state of cessation. Having certainty in that way is the mental engagement with the aspect of the Truth of the Path. Regarding the detailed explanation of the division of the five paths: there are two parts, the instruction on the sequence of the path of ordinary beings and the instruction on the arya path along with its fruit. The first includes the instruction on the qualities associated with the path of accumulation, and the instruction on the qualities associated with the path of preparation. Regarding the first, the instruction that one must rely primarily on ethics and wisdom on the path of accumulation is as follows: Even persons endowed with caste, form, and learning are not respected if they lack wisdom and ethics. Therefore, whoever possesses these two qualities, even if they lack other virtues, is worthy of worship. Whatever persons may have become the king’s caste, like a great sala tree, or the brahmin’s caste, like a great sala tree—thus having become of the highest caste—possessing fine form such as being beautiful and free of illness, and having undergone extensive training in the eighteen sciences and other conventional studies—if they lack the wisdom to act according to the nature of reality and to know the path of liberation, and lack the ethics of abiding in purified conduct of what to accept and what to reject, they are not objects of respect and worship for the world, including the gods. Furthermore, if one has caste, form, and learning...

<meta>continues from previous page: are still stuck in a state of "having an attainment," so how is this different from the old ways? Furthermore, this is even worse than before. Why? Because you previously held onto the old interpretations of the Treatise on Numbers, and now you have added the "new wisdom" of the Three Treatises. This is just adding another layer of views. The Master said: "This is merely adding feet to a snake." It can be said that the more one learns, the more inverted one becomes. The intention of the scriptures and treatises is to quiet the mind and reach the original source, which is why we are called <term>shramana</term> <gloss>ascetics/monastics</gloss>. Moreover, this quieting must reach the point where there is no more quieting. Regarding the claim that one does not need to refute the "Middle-Provisional," those who embody the Way understand that this "provisional nature" is originally the Way itself; there is no need to refute it. If one insists on refuting it, is one not then refuting the Way? One must see this point deeply. The reason we speak of "refutation" now is that these people do not know that the "provisional nature" they established is originally the Way; they mistake the Way for "not-the-Way." We now simply guide them to realize that "not-the-Way" is actually the Way. Therefore, we speak of refutation, but in reality, there is no refutation. Secondly, one must understand that nature is precisely the provisional. Ordinary people, in their delusion, say that the provisional forms a nature. The Buddhas observe that nature is always provisional. Therefore, it is said that all worldly truths, when viewed by the Tathagata...

are always the supreme truth. Thirdly, those who embody the Way know that this Way was never a provisional nature.

# The Dragon Plays with the Spider

A hunter was lying in wait in the mountains at night when he saw a small person, about two feet tall, walking alone along the bottom of a ravine. A short time later, another person appeared, similar in height. As they met, they asked each other where they were going. The first one said, "I am going to pay a visit to Old Scar Yang. I have seen that his complexion is dim and dark, indicating bad luck." The second one replied, "I am doing the same. What you say is true." The hunter, realizing they were not human, shouted loudly at them. Both figures vanished instantly. That night, he captured a fox; in the middle of its forehead was a scar as large as a coin.

# The Dragon Plays with the Spider

Mr. Xu served in the joint office of Qidong. There was a building used to store provisions, but things were often stolen, leaving a mess on the floor. The household staff were frequently scolded, so they lay in wait to keep watch. They saw a spider as large as a bushel basket. Terrified, they fled and reported it to Mr. Xu. He considered it strange, and from that day on, he sent his servants to feed it. The spider became increasingly tame; whenever it was hungry, it would come out and rely on...

<summary>A hunter encounters two supernatural beings discussing a man's impending bad luck, followed by the introduction of a giant spider kept by Mr. Xu.</summary>
<keywords>supernatural, spider, hunter, omen, Qidong</keywords>
</translation>

<translation page="166">
...the person to be fed before leaving. More than a year passed. One day, Mr. Xu was reviewing documents when the spider suddenly came and crouched under his desk. Suspecting it was hungry, he called his servants to bring food. Suddenly, he saw two snakes pinning the spider down, winding around it like chopsticks. The spider curled its legs and retracted its abdomen as if it could not withstand the fear. In a split second, the snakes grew suddenly, becoming as thick as eggs. Terrified, he wanted to run away, when a massive thunderclap occurred. The whole household was shaken. After a long while, Mr. Xu regained consciousness. His wife and servants were struck dead, numbering seven or eight. Mr. Xu fell ill for over a month and eventually died. Mr. Xu was a man of integrity and honesty who loved his people dearly. When the news of his death spread, the people collected money to see him off, and the sound of wailing filled the countryside.

Wu Shishi says: I always thought "The Dragon Plays with the Spider" was just a rumor from the streets. Can it be that such a thing actually exists? I have heard that thunder strikes are always aimed at wicked people. Why then did such an upright and good official suffer this cruel tragedy? Is the resentment of the Heavens truly so unrestrained?

<note>Wu Shishi was a commentator on Pu Songling's work, often providing moral or skeptical reflections on the tales.</note>

<summary>The giant spider is attacked by snakes, triggering a supernatural thunder strike that kills the magistrate and his household, followed by a commentator's reflection on the injustice of the tragedy.</summary>
<keywords>thunder, snakes, tragedy, integrity, commentary, Wu Shishi</keywords>
</translation>

<header>Imperially Commissioned Complete Library of the Four Treasuries</header>

To "know words" is to be able to discern the right and wrong in people's speech; to "exhaust the principles" of things is for the heart to be like a clear mirror, and only then can one observe people as the Sage does.

○ The Master said: "Reviewing the old and learning the new, one may become a teacher."

"Reviewing" means to search out and trace. "Old" refers to what one has previously heard; "new" refers to what one has just grasped. If one can practice what was previously learned and consistently gain new insights, then the knowledge remains within oneself, and one's capacity to respond becomes inexhaustible, which is why one can be a teacher. As for <margin>pronounced *fú*</margin> "learning for the sake of repeating and asking questions," <note>referring to rote memorization without internal reflection</note> one gains nothing within the heart <margin>Master Chen of Xin'an says: [compared] with</margin>, and what one knows is limited. <margin>Master Chen of Xin'an says: [compared] with</margin> This is the opposite of having an inexhaustible capacity to respond. The *Record of Learning* <note>original: "Xueji" (a chapter in the Classic of Rites)</note> criticizes such learning as insufficient to make one a teacher, which perfectly complements the meaning here. <margin>Zhu Xi says: Learning for the sake of repeating [is not the same as] reviewing the old and</margin> If one does not search for the principles inside oneself, then memorizing ten things results in only ten things, and memorizing a hundred results in only a hundred; this makes learning dead and stagnant. "Learning the new" means finding insights within what was already reviewed.

<meta>Volume 2</meta>
<summary>This page discusses the method of observing people by discerning their words and understanding universal principles, while explaining the Master's teaching on the necessity of both reviewing old knowledge and deriving new insights to qualify as a teacher.</summary>
<keywords>Knowing words, Exhausting principles, Reviewing the old, Learning the new, Rote memorization</keywords>
</translation>

<translation page="51">
<margin>Complete Commentaries on the Analects</margin>

This principle becomes more refined, surpassing what it was before. By extending and expanding upon it, and by inferring from one case to others, the knowledge remains active and not dead. In the *Doctrine of the Mean*, "reviewing the old and learning the new" does not mean reviewing the old *or* learning the new; rather, it is reviewing the old to attain the new. If one pursues the new without reviewing the old, one cannot know the new. If one is not sufficient to be a teacher, it is because one has severed the path; if one truly does not review the old, one is also insufficient to be a teacher. The meaning of this statement lies in "learning the new." It is only by reviewing the old that one can learn the new. The "new" is not a separate principle. When one practices repeatedly until familiar, insights gradually emerge. For instance, the principles themselves are all things we inquire into; when a person asks about a principle, it is like seeing several people inquire about it, and from that principle, one derives further understanding. One's capacity to respond is then endless. "Learning for the sake of repeating and asking questions," by contrast, means that if one remembers one thing, one says one thing, and it never goes beyond that. This deviates from the principle of reviewing the old to reach the new. This is the logic of "learning below and penetrating above." <note>A reference to Analects 14.35, implying basic study leads to higher understanding of heaven.</note> That is to say, this single principle is what is recorded in the Six Classics, and it is the same principle recorded in the Analects and the Mencius. When one constantly reviews and practices, one realizes the flavor is profound and lasting, and one naturally acquires new insights. It is also said: What was previously understood...

<summary>This page continues the discussion on the synergy between reviewing past knowledge and discovering new insights, emphasizing that true understanding is a living, internal process rather than mere rote memorization.</summary>
<keywords>Doctrine of the Mean, Learning, Principles, Analects, Mencius</keywords>
</translation>

<header>Comprehensive Guide to Arithmetic and Geometry</header>
<meta>41</meta>
3 multiplied again is 27, and multiplied again is 64. For a fifth power of 64/25, use 2/3 as the origin; multiplying the number 3 by 5 gives 15, and multiplying the number 2 by 5 gives 6. ...and thus the accounts of Huan were passed down. The Marquis of Chen said to Zigong, "Only now do I know the value of a sage." Zigong replied, "It is not as good as mastering his Way and implementing his transformative influence." <margin>Revised to say: "It is better."</margin>

After Yang Huo fled to Qi, he went from Qi to Jin and joined the Zhao family. When Confucius heard of this, he said to Zilu, "The Zhao family will surely have chaos in their generation." Zilu asked, "Power does not reside with him, so how could he cause chaos?" Confucius replied, "This is not something you would know. Yang Huo is close to those in power but not close to benevolence. He held favor with Jisun and even attempted to kill him. Failing that, he fled to Qi, and when the people of Qi imprisoned him, he escaped to Jin. Thus, both the states of Qi and Lu have rid themselves of a malady. Zhao Jianzi is greedy for profit and fond of killing. He will surely favor [Yang Huo's] theories and follow his plots. The disasters and failures that follow will not be limited to a single generation; this is predictable."

Ji Kangzi asked Confucius, "In the current twelfth month of the Zhou calendar, which corresponds to the tenth month of the Xia calendar, there are still locusts. Why is this?" Confucius replied, "I have heard that creatures hibernate only after the fire star <note>referring to Antares, which marks the season</note> has descended. Now, the fire star is still moving toward the west." <margin>The Zhengqi Hall edition</margin>
</translation>

<translation page="62">
It is a mistake of the calendar official. Ji Kangzi asked, "How many months have been lost?" Confucius replied, "In the tenth month of the Xia calendar, the fire star should have already set. Seeing it now means the intercalary month has been missed again." <margin>See the Zuo Zhuan, 12th year of Duke Ai.</margin>

King Fuchai of Wu intended to use Duke Ai to meet with the Marquis of Jin. Zifu Jingbo said to the envoy, "When the King gathers the feudal lords, the Hegemon leads the lords and keepers of the land to meet with the King. When the Hegemon gathers the feudal lords, the lords lead the viscounts and barons to meet with the Hegemon. Now, the feudal lords are meeting, and the King intends to have our humble ruler meet with the ruler of Jin, which would make Jin the de facto Hegemon. Moreover, if you, sir, summon the lords in the name of the Hegemon but use the lords to perform the service, what benefit is there in this?" The people of Wu then desisted. Later, however, they regretted it and imprisoned Jingbo. Jingbo said to the Grand Minister Pi, "Lu is about to hold ceremonies for the Supreme Deity and the former kings on the first *xin* day of the tenth month, finishing on the third *xin* day. In what generation has there been such a dereliction of duty? Since the founding of Lu, this has never been changed. If we do not attend, the masters of prayer and the ancestral temples will say that Wu is truly without ritual." [Pi] spoke to Fuchai and sent him home. When Zigong heard this, he met with Confucius and said, "The son of the Zifu clan is clumsy in his speech."
</translation>

If the person has the ability to obtain the object, let them obtain it; if they cannot, one should not hesitate to use methods to supply it. For those who are poor and cannot afford wealth, one might borrow from the rich or falsely claim to be a relative or friend, then place the funds at the bedside to provide them with joy. This is the primary method for treating the illness of poverty. For those who have not yet obtained official rank, one may either urgently pay the grain contribution <note>a practice of purchasing official titles through donations of grain</note> for them or falsely claim that they have been recommended for a post. For those who already hold office, one may either truly plot for their appointment to a post or falsely report a promotion. For elderly people who desire to increase their longevity, one may produce words from the mouths of astrologers or shaman-physicians to comfort them. Why should I be stingy with such words? This is the method of "using the person's own ways to treat the person himself." However, although treating other illnesses is easy, treating poverty is difficult. In this world, those who worry about poverty and fall ill, whose illnesses are beyond saving, are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. If one could borrow the grain of the Great Granary <note>referring to state-owned grain reserves</note> or loan the gold of Guo Kuang <note>a historical figure known for his extreme wealth</note>, everyone would be a Jiezi Garden <note>the name of Li Yu's residence, implying a place of generosity</note>.

### The Third Category: Medicine of Deep Affection

The third category is that a person to whom one is deeply attached can serve as medicine. In human hearts, private affection is always focused on someone. Often, a ruler cannot obtain it from a minister, or a father cannot obtain it from a son; yet, a very distant and unlovable person may become the focus of one’s spirit and the very thing upon which one’s life depends. This is an object of deep emotional attachment. It may be a charming wife or beautiful concubine, a close companion or a youthful page, or a very dear and intimate friend. When one thinks of them but cannot have them, or has them but cannot be near them, this can cause illness. Even for someone who has fallen ill for other reasons, when they are at a point of physical pain and spiritual desolation, they will surely think of their beloved. Suddenly bringing them together is like a fish finding water; there has never been a case where the ears do not clear, the eyes do not brighten, and the spirit does not become suddenly robust.
</translation>

<summary>Li Yu discusses using material aid to treat the "illness of poverty" and the therapeutic power of being reunited with a deeply beloved person to restore health and spirit.</summary>
<keywords>poverty, social support, emotional attachment, companionship, healing, psychology</keywords>

<header>Essentials of Buddhist Study</header>

Fayu heard of this from afar. He took a bamboo tube, placed a bramble staff inside, sealed it, and sent it to Fayu. When Fayu opened the seal and saw the staff, he immediately said, "This is because of the monk who drank alcohol. My teaching and guidance have not been diligent, and I have caused concern to be bestowed upon me from afar." He then struck the wooden bell to gather the assembly. He placed the tube in front of them, burned incense, and paid respects. He prostrated on the ground and ordered the <term>weinuo</term> <gloss>temple administrator</gloss> to strike him three times with the staff. He wept and reproached himself. Everyone, both monastic and lay within the region, was moved to sigh. Because of this, many were inspired to cultivate their practice with greater effort.

> Eulogy: Alas. If people today were to open the elder An’s package, few would refrain from smashing the tube, breaking the staff, and speaking wildly. A holy teacher and a virtuous disciple. Even a thousand years later, I still hold these two men in high regard.

### Performing Repentance for the Teacher

During the Jin dynasty, Fakuang was from Xiapi. He lost his parents at a young age and was known for his filial service to his stepmother. Later, he left the home life and studied under the monk Tanyin. Once, Tanyin became critically ill. Fakuang prayed with sincerity and performed rites of repentance for seven days and seven nights. On the seventh day, he suddenly saw a five-colored light shining upon the doors and windows of Tanyin’s room. Tanyin felt as if someone had shaken him with their hand, and his ailment was healed.

### Standing in Snow Past the Knees

During the Wei dynasty, Shenguang’s scholarly understanding surpassed the world. When Grandmaster Bodhidharma arrived from the Western Regions, he went to study under him. Bodhidharma did not speak to him. One evening, there was a great snowfall. Shenguang stood in the courtyard until dawn, and the snow reached his knees. Bodhidharma looked at him and said, "You have stood in the snow for a long time; what is it that you seek?" Shenguang wept and said, "I only wish for the Master to open the gate of nectar <note>meaning: the gate of the Dharma/Enlightenment</note> and broadly liberate all beings." Bodhidharma said, "The supreme, wonderful path of the Buddhas requires diligent application over countless <term>kalpas</term> <gloss>cosmic ages</gloss>. It requires doing what is difficult to do and enduring what is difficult to endure. Even then, one may not reach it. You, with a light and shallow mind, wish to hope for the true vehicle? You labor in vain." Hearing this instruction, Shenguang...</translation>

<translation page="25">
<header>Records of Exalted Conduct in the Buddhist Order: The Conduct of Respecting the Teacher, Part Three</header>

...was encouraged. He took a blade and severed his arm, placing it before Bodhidharma. Bodhidharma said, "Those who seek the Buddha’s path forget their physical form for the sake of the Dharma. Now that you have severed your arm, your seeking may indeed be possible." Shenguang said, "My mind is not yet at peace. I beg the Master to pacify my mind." Bodhidharma said, "Bring your mind here, and I will pacify it for you." Shenguang said, "I have searched for my mind, and it cannot be found." Bodhidharma said, "I have finished pacifying your mind for you." He then transmitted the Dharma, and Shenguang became the <term>Second Patriarch</term> <gloss>of the Chan school</gloss>.

> Eulogy: The Second Patriarch obtained the Dharma because of his sincere devotion. When the conditions were ripe, it happened just like that. They met like a needle and a mustard seed <note>a metaphor for a perfect, destined connection</note>. It was not necessarily the severing of the arm that caused this. Foolish people who imitate this will only end up using knives and chopping blocks. Alas. If the transmission of the Dharma required severing an arm, none of the Patriarchs would have intact skin. If the attainment of Buddhahood required burning one’s body, there would be no holy ones left. Sever the arm of afflictions, and burn the body of ignorance. I urge practitioners of Chan to strive for this.

### ->Leaving the Teacher and Repenting<-

During the Tang dynasty, Qingjiang realized the illusory nature of life at a young age. He paid respects to the Vinaya Master Tanyi as his personal teacher. He recited the scriptures and mastered them at a glance. Those who recognized his talent said, "This is a thousand-league steed of the Buddhist order." Once, he disagreed slightly with his teacher, left him, and traveled to study elsewhere. After visiting many Dharma assemblies, he reproached himself, saying, "Having traveled half the world, I find that those like my original teacher are rare." He then returned. When the monks were gathered at his teacher’s place, he carried a bramble branch on his back and declared, "I, <term>Moujia</term> <gloss>a humble self-reference</gloss>, once again throw myself upon the Master. I only wish to be accepted." At that time, the Master scolded him. Qingjiang wept, repented, and apologized, saying, "Previously, I acted out of ignorance; now, my mind has realized the truth. I hope the Master will use his great compassion to grant me joy." He pleaded again and again. Master Tanyi took pity on him, and they became teacher and disciple as before. After Tanyi passed away, he exhausted his efforts under National Master Zhong and secretly received the transmission of the heart-essence.

> Eulogy: To realize one's mistake after abandoning a sage, and to remain steadfast despite scolding—this is truly clarity and sincerity. Did he not receive the heart-seal in the end because of this? Those of shallow faith leave without returning at the slightest grievance. They harbor resentment forever at the slightest rebuke. What is the point of meeting a brilliant teacher? It is like meeting an emperor and failing to secure a single position. What a pity.

<summary>This page describes the profound dedication of disciples, including the extreme devotion of the Second Patriarch Shenguang and the remorseful return of the monk Qingjiang, highlighting the virtue of humility and persistence in the teacher-disciple relationship.</summary>
<keywords>Bodhidharma, Shenguang, Qingjiang, Tanyi, repentance, transmission of Dharma, teacher-disciple relationship, humility</keywords></translation>

<meta>continues from previous page: ...Wind above the lake, the image of Inner Truth. The superior person embodies the virtue of Heaven and Earth in cherishing life, and therefore deliberates on punishments and delays executions.</meta>

The meaning of <term>Inner Truth</term> <gloss>Zhong Fu</gloss> lies here. When a legal case is about to be concluded, one deliberates on it; when a sentence is about to be carried out, one delays it. Only in this way can one satisfy the human heart. To speak of a case while also speaking of "deliberation" is to seek the path of life within the midst of a death sentence. To speak of execution while also speaking of "delay" is to seek the spark of life within the death penalty.

Emperor Shun <note>legendary sage-king</note> showed compassion in his punishments; Yu the Great <note>legendary sage-king who controlled the floods</note> wept over the crimes of others; Tang <note>founder of the Shang dynasty</note> prayed to open the nets <note>a reference to Tang's mercy in hunting, where he removed three sides of the net to allow animals to escape</note>; King Wen covered the bleaching bones <note>King Wen of Zhou performed rites for the unburied dead out of compassion</note>. If these actions did not arise from the sincerity of the original heart, who would have been moved by them? When the King hears a case, the Three Excellencies hear it; when the Three Excellencies hear it, the Minister of Justice hears it; this is the deliberation of punishments. Every ten days the officials listen, and every thirty days they report to the ruler; this is the delay of executions. Deliberating on punishments follows the image of <term>Dui</term> <gloss>Joy</gloss>; delaying executions follows the image of <term>Gen</term> <gloss>Stillness/Stopping</gloss>. Considering the one hexagram and its six lines, it is the image of being empty in the center.

Considering the two trigrams <note>upper and lower</note>, and the second and fifth lines, it is the image of being solid in the center. Both are images of inner truth. <term>Inner Truth</term> is trust residing in the heart. Trust residing in the heart is trust residing in principle. To see principle and trust it is the way to have trust residing in the heart. Among the sixty-four hexagrams, there is not one hexagram or one line that does not take trust as its pivot. Without trust, the center cannot be empty; how then could it be solid? Being empty allows for solidity, as the yielding line trusts in the firm line. To be joyous while remaining still is how one achieves emptiness. Trust reaching to the pigs and fish is the result of empty hearts responding to one another. Boarding a wooden boat is the result of emptiness helping emptiness. Its reality is simply principle. Principle is Heaven. It is that which makes the heart the heart. It is what is meant by "beneficial for remaining correct."

# High-minded individuals naturally possess the means to rectify matters

## Instructions for Dong Zhiguang

Student Dong was born and raised in a wealthy household, yet early on he developed a heart set on transcending birth and death. This is likely the result of the internal influence of his past karmic connections to the <term>prajna</term> <gloss>transcendent wisdom</gloss>. He previously visited Master Yunqi, who taught him the Pure Land method. Recently, he visited this old man <note>referring to the author, Hanshan Deqing</note> at Shuangjing, expressing his desire to receive the <term>upasaka</term> <gloss>lay Buddhist</gloss> precepts and to openly confess his deep and heavy karmic offenses. He asked for the essential method to escape suffering and for how to practice in order to eradicate his transgressions. I, the old man, instructed him, saying: "When a student recognizes that the roots of their offenses are deep, the ancient masters teach them to eliminate old karma at all times and strictly avoid creating new disasters. The Buddha opened the gate of repentance for sentient beings burdened with heavy karma, which is the most convenient method for escaping suffering." A verse says:

> All offenses are like frost and dew,
> The sun of wisdom can eliminate them.
> If one wishes to repent,
> Sit upright and contemplate true reality.

This is the primary practice; all else is but auxiliary and convenient means. The true nature of sentient beings is, with the Buddha...
</translation>

<translation page="11">
<header>Mengyou Collection, Volume 3</header>

<page-num>5</page-num>

equal and inherently unstained, nor does it possess the characteristics of birth, death, coming, or going. It is only because, from the very beginning, one is not enlightened, that one is deluded about their own self-nature; therefore, it is called ignorance <term>avidya</term>. Because of ignorance, all kinds of false thoughts arise, leading to various delusions and the creation of different types of karma. One falsely clings to the suffering of birth and death within the three realms. All of this arises because ignorance fails to understand one's own mind, and one follows the turnings of false thoughts. It is like a person in a deep sleep, experiencing various evil dreams, various states, and various terrors, enduring unbearable sufferings. When they finally wake up, they look for the events of the dream, but they are utterly unattainable. Therefore, sentient beings are fallen into the dream of ignorance, following false thoughts and delusions, creating various karma, and bringing suffering upon themselves. If you look at it with eyes awakened, can the states of these delusions truly be found? Now, while currently in this dream of ignorance, how can one eliminate old karma? One must use the light of wisdom to illuminate and break through ignorance, and believe that one's own mind is inherently pure and not driven by false thoughts and delusions. Then, all karma will be without cause, for false thoughts are the cause of all karma. Why is this? Because from beginningless time, one has been deluded about one's own original mind, life after life...
</translation>

<summary>These pages contain moral and practical instruction for a lay practitioner named Dong Zhiguang, emphasizing the necessity of repentance and the realization of the mind's inherent purity to overcome the delusions of ignorance.</summary>
<keywords>Repentance, Pure Land, Ignorance, True Reality, Karma, Wisdom, Delusion, Self-nature</keywords>

<translation page="120">
<meta>continues from previous page: ...The concept of the generation and overcoming of the five elements is deeply detrimental to correct principles.</meta>
<header>From the discourse on "less by one jin"</header>

Water, fire, earth, and stone constitute the body and function of heaven and earth, standing distinctly apart from the views of other schools. Master Zhang <note>Zhang Zai</note> says in his *Zhengmeng* <gloss>Correcting Youthful Ignorance</gloss> that water and fire are <term>qi</term> <gloss>vital energy</gloss>. Therefore, their tendency to flame upward and moisten downward, and the ascending and descending of <term>yin</term> and <term>yang</term>, cannot be controlled by earth. Wood and metal are the flowers and fruits of earth. Their nature contains a mixture of water and fire. As for the substance of wood, it grows when soaked in water and burns in fire, yet it does not abandon these properties. This is because it obtains the flowers of earth and floats at the intersection of water and fire. As for the substance of metal, it obtains the essence of fire from the dryness of earth and the essence of water from the dampness of earth. Thus, water and fire wait upon one another and do not harm each other. When melted, metal flows back into liquid but does not diminish. This is because it obtains the solid essence of earth at the threshold of water and fire. Earth is that by which things are brought to their beginning and brought to their end. It is the substance of the earth and the end of transformation. It is that by which water and fire ascend and descend.

<summary>This page analyzes the nature of the five elements as described by Zhang Zai, specifically focusing on the interactions between water, fire, earth, wood, and metal as manifestations of qi.</summary>
<keywords>Water and Fire, Five Elements, Zhang Zai, Zhengmeng, Qi</keywords>
</translation>

Abu al-Hasan and Umar Bali have retracted their rulings of permissibility and now follow the fatwa of the Mufti, Shaykh Muhammad Sa'id Babasil. They acknowledge that the Mufti's fatwa represents the Shafi'i school of thought, in which there is no disagreement among the scholars of the Shafi'i school. This is the evidence. According to the response of the Mufti, that which is in the Shafi'i school is established without disagreement within the school. From this, it is known that the fatwa of those who contradicted the Mufti's fatwa is invalid. Therefore, all those who issued a fatwa contradicting the aforementioned fatwa have retracted their positions, acknowledged their errors, and have had their signatures written above, confirming the fatwa of the Mufti <note>so that it may be known by the brothers</note> who see this response. Ahmad Khatib, Imam of the Shafi'is in Makkah, from the Sacred Mosque <note>al-Masjid al-Haram</note>. [The] head of the Mentawai community, Haji Marzuki, confirms the fatwa of the Mufti, Shaykh Muhammad Sa'id Babasil, and invalidates the
<page-break/>
fatwa of those who ruled it permissible to sell pigs to the Chinese. This is the evidence.
Praise be to Allah alone, and peace and blessings be upon the one after whom there is no prophet.

He has seen the fatwa of the Shaykh al-Islam and Mufti of mankind, Shaykh Muhammad Sa'id Babasil, and several Shafi'i scholars who signed below that fatwa, stating that it is firmly prohibited to sell pigs to the Chinese according to the correct opinion in the Shafi'i school, and the words of those who claimed it was permissible are invalid. And Allah knows best. The head of the Mentawai community, Haji Marzuki bin Haji Ismail, signed it. He, who is weak and lowly, seeks help from Allah the Glorified and Exalted, who grants guidance. Guidance for the correctness of the fatwa, that is in the year 1317 <note>Hijri</note>. Praised be the leaders of the scholars in Makkah, and may Allah reward them with a great reward and keep them in a noble position. O Allah, grant us success in following them in religion. Amen, Lord of the worlds. Thus, praise be to Allah and thanks be to Allah, and peace and blessings.

Fatwa
</translation>

<translation page="17">
upon the best of Allah's creation, and upon his family and companions, the guides of the community, and upon the scholars who are their inheritors, and those who follow them until the Day of Resurrection. And after: In Makkah, in the year of the Prophet's Hijra <note>1317</note>, I issued a fatwa in Belibuo, Affdeling Mentawai, regarding the prohibition of selling pigs to the Chinese. After I investigated the matter, some of them rejected my fatwa. Their leader, [a man named Madi bin Macan], sent a letter to Haji Abu al-Hasan of Palembang, Talu Bali Makkah. Haji Abu al-Hasan replied, and he also obtained a response from two people, namely Muhammad Mansuri Maliki and Umar Bali Ampunan. [Haji Abu al-Hasan then immediately issued a fatwa of permissibility for Haji Madi bin Macan, and he claimed that he had already inquired with the Mufti Sayyid Ahmad bin Zaini Dahlan previously, and the Mufti had ruled it permissible, and he had already asked this current Mufti, namely Shaykh Muhammad Sa'id Babasil, and the Mufti had ruled it permissible. He also reported that Muhammad Mansuri
<page-break/>
Maliki and Umar Bali Ampunan likewise permitted it in Makkah.] The letter of Haji Abu al-Hasan in Makkah to Haji Madi bin Macan in Belibuo. Then Haji Dat Mentawai [Radin Muhammad Arif Boyan] returned the letter of Haji Abu al-Hasan and sent a copy to the Penghulu of Penang. [He] then immediately sent his letter to Makkah to the leader, the head of the Mentawai community, Haji Marzuki. Then, on Friday, 8 Ramadan [1323], the head of the Mentawai community, Haji Marzuki, showed the letter of Haji Abu al-Hasan from Makkah, informing him that he had issued a fatwa of permissibility for selling pigs to the Chinese, and that the fatwa of the Mufti Sayyid Ahmad Dahlan was also permissible, and that the fatwa of the Mufti Shaykh Muhammad Sa'id Babasil was also permissible, and following it were the two response letters from Mansuri Maliki and the response of Umar Bali, both letters signed and both issuing a fatwa of permissibility. It was further mentioned that Haji Abu al-Hasan requested that the head of the community bring those two response letters to Belibuo so that their meaning could be clarified to the people of Belibuo, so that the people would not be deceived.
</translation>

<summary>This text documents the retraction of fatwas regarding the sale of pigs to the Chinese by local figures, following the authoritative Shafi'i ruling issued by Shaykh Muhammad Sa'id Babasil, confirmed by Shaykh Ahmad Khatib al-Minangkabawi and local leaders in Mentawai.</summary>
<keywords>Fatwa, Shafi'i school, Prohibition, Pig trade, Mentawai, Shaykh Muhammad Sa'id Babasil, Ahmad Khatib al-Minangkabawi</keywords>

<translation page="20">In this, the male and female are equal because they are the mother’s brothers and sisters, and the uterine brothers are on the father’s side along with their sisters, as is known. If they were to divide the inheritance of the son of a uterine sister and the maternal uncles and aunts from her, they would not divide it such that the male receives the share of two females. End quote.

It is apparent from both the <term>Tuhfa</term> <gloss>a prominent Shafi'i legal text by Ibn Hajar al-Haytami</gloss> and the <term>Nihaya</term> <gloss>another major Shafi'i legal text by al-Ramli</gloss> that their statement "they are divided equally" is a restriction applying to both the children of the uterine descendants and the maternal uncles and aunts from her. That is explicit in the <term>Sharh al-Rawd</term> <gloss>Commentary on the Rawd al-Talib by Zakariyya al-Ansari</gloss>, as you have learned from its wording. However, the matter is not like that; rather, their statement "equally" is a restriction applying only to the children of the uterine descendants. The exception is clear then. They then mentioned the aspect of the exception until they said: "As for the maternal uncles and aunts from the mother—meaning the sisters of the deceased’s mother and her sisters on her mother’s side—they are excluded from the aforementioned rule, as you have learned." If they were to inherit the mother’s share as if she were the deceased, they would divide it according to the number of their heads.</translation>

I understood it as such, so that we do not rule that this was an oversight. End. And God knows best. If the male and female are from the same side, such as the children of the daughter, and are in the same degree, and one of them preceded the other to the heir, he is given priority through it. Otherwise, they inherit through both. Like the daughter of the daughter of a daughter of a son of a daughter, if the son of the daughter of Zayd were to marry his other granddaughter, he would produce a daughter. And the daughter of a sister on the father’s side, who is the daughter of a uterine brother, if the brother of Zayd on his mother’s side were to marry his sister on his father’s side, he would produce a daughter. The Tsarevich lay on the floor unconscious, the Tsar in an armchair, also almost in a faint.

And with God is the success to return to the truth. Amen.

### The Ninth Matter: Clarifying the argument for the impermissibility of multiplication in this specific case.
It is not hidden from any knowledgeable person that our Shafi’i Imams, may God be pleased with them, only permitted the multiplication of Friday prayers due to the existence of need and necessity, which is the certainty of difficulty in gathering, as will come from *al-Tuhfah*, in order to avert the embarrassment resulting from hardship that is unbearable. It is known that every necessity is measured by its extent. They established reasons for the difficulty in gathering, whether due to fighting, the narrowness of the place due to the multitude of worshippers, or the distance of the town's peripheries. They established for each of these reasons limiting conditions that must be present with certainty. The condition for the narrowness of the place is that it is certain that there is no place in the town of the Friday prayer that can accommodate them. Furthermore, the reliable position, as in *al-Tuhfah* and *al-Nihayah*, is that the standard is based on those whose attendance at the Friday prayer is expected, not those who actually attended, whether the place is a mosque or otherwise. Thus, the certainty of the absence of a place is established by the actual absence of any place for the Friday prayer, the impossibility of expanding the place that has become narrow, and the impossibility of roofing that which is unroofed if the prayer is in the sun

<meta>catchword: is obtained</meta>

<column-break/>

from which a hardship that is certainly unbearable is obtained. Thus, the absence of what is mentioned here with certainty is the [same] impossibility that our master al-Ghazali pointed to by his statement: "If their gathering in one mosque is impossible, it is permitted in two mosques," etc. For the meaning of impossibility is the total lack of possibility, not merely the speculation of a lack of space, nor the mere claim of narrowness without verification of the aforementioned meaning with certainty, but rather guessing at the unseen and seeking comfort and luxury. Furthermore, the condition of the distance of the periphery is either that the distance is from dawn until the time of the Friday prayer, or that the call to prayer cannot be heard from it, as explained in the seventh matter, or the presence of hardship that is unbearable in the meaning mentioned in the eighth matter. Thus, the certainty of the difficulty of gathering is not achieved except with these mentioned restrictions and conditions. Therefore, the statement of *al-Tuhfah*, "and the difficulty of their gathering with certainty," means by the presence of one of those reasons with its conditions. Likewise is every statement of al-Ghazali. And when the need is verified—that is, by the presence of what we mentioned—for they have defined the difficulty of gathering resulting from one of those reasons by the hardship that is unbearable. He said in *al-Tuhfah*: "The standard for difficulty is that it contains a hardship that is unbearable." The end. And this hardship is that which contains embarrassment and necessity, as mentioned in the eighth matter, and it will come here from al-Qamuli, clarifying that with its evidence. Among the legal opinions of our master, Sayyid Abdallah bin Umar bin Yahya, is that al-Qamuli, in *al-Jawahir*, when mentioning the permissibility of multiplication due to difficulty, supported it with the Quranic verse: "He has not placed upon you any difficulty in the religion," which indicates that our permission for the scholars to multiply is to negate embarrassment. The end, with omission. This is also a clarification that the presence of embarrassment and necessity is what is meant by the hardship</translation>

<translation page="13">that is unbearable, which is the standard for the difficulty of gathering that permits multiplication. For it has become a habit to consider the hardship of going to the mosque as a search for comfort and luxury. **So, when you have known** and verified all that is mentioned here, and known what was mentioned in the fifth matter regarding the description of the old mosque, its vastness, and the vastness of its courtyard, you will know and verify at that time the absence of the cause permitting multiplication, which is the absence of a place that accommodates them—that is, those whose attendance is expected, as was mentioned that this is the reliable position according to Ibn Hajar, al-Ramli, and others. That is because of the vastness of this mentioned mosque and the vastness of its courtyard, according to the sight of it. **And when you have known** what was mentioned in the seventh matter regarding the distance between the two mosques, that there is no hardship in it that is unbearable in its meaning mentioned in the eighth matter, and that the call to prayer is heard between the two ends of the neighborhoods of the two mosques, let alone that they are distant by the distance of between the time of dawn and the time of the Friday prayer, **you will know** and verify at that time the absence of the cause permitting multiplication, which is the distance of the periphery, due to the close distance between the two ends of the neighborhoods of the two mosques, with the absence of the aforementioned hardship. **Thus it appears** and becomes clear to you now, by what has been mentioned and what has been written, that the case at hand does not permit the multiplication of Friday prayers, for the absence of any of its causes is certain, let alone the certainty of the existence of any of them. Thus, all the texts of the Imams stating the permissibility of multiplication with its conditions cannot be used as evidence for the permissibility of multiplication in this case, which is devoid of those conditions. Similarly, the response of the Mufti of Makkah cannot be taken as evidence for the validity of multiplication in this case, because it contains the mention of the condition of need and hardship which

none of it was found in the case itself, as has been established in these matters repeatedly. And it will be known clearly from the eleventh matter to come. — 413 —

The ministers are clever, but Alexander Nikolaevich <note>Tsar Alexander II</note> does not trust them fully. To assist them, he has called upon the famous Doctor Liprandi <note>Pavel Liprandi, a general known for his severe administrative and punitive measures</note>, who prescribes heroic remedies and will undoubtedly hasten a tragedy. The great consolation of the ruling Petersburg elite is now the people and the people's attachment to the Tsar. They threaten the revolutionary youth with the people. "The Tsar has only to wave his hand, and there will be no more students." Yes, undoubtedly they will be gone; but on the very next day, there will be no nobility left in all of Russia, and along with the nobility, the entire bureaucracy will perish under the axe; you yourselves, my dears, will perish. Well, just try waving your hand! And there will remain only the people and the Tsar. And what will this Tsar do with this people? Our Tsar is, after all, bureaucratic and noble, not a *Zemsky* <gloss>representative of the land/people</gloss> ruler.
